question: The excess cadmium accumulation in our body, damages which part of the body?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Liver and kidneys**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cadmium** is a toxic heavy metal that can accumulate in the human body through various means such as food, water, and air.
 
• Once cadmium enters the body, it is primarily stored in the **liver and kidneys**.
 
• Excessive accumulation of cadmium in these organs can lead to severe damage and dysfunction.
 
• The **kidneys** are particularly vulnerable because cadmium can disrupt their ability to filter waste from the blood, leading to kidney disease.
 
• The **liver** can also be affected as cadmium can cause liver damage, impairing its ability to detoxify the body and produce essential proteins.
 
• Cadmium exposure is linked to various health issues such as **osteoporosis, cardiovascular diseases, and cancer**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hands and feet**__

 __
 
• While cadmium exposure can cause peripheral neuropathy leading to tingling or numbness in hands and feet, it is not the primary site of cadmium accumulation.
 
 
 
• **Eye**__
 __
 
• Cadmium exposure can affect vision but it is not a primary site for cadmium accumulation.
 
 
 
• **Stomach**__
 
 
• Cadmium can cause gastrointestinal distress when ingested, but it does not accumulate in the stomach.
